title: Worked Examples: Lost Days at the Dosing on Record (Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit)
content:
**Rule.** For a lost, stolen or damaged medication replacement under the Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit, the lost days are counted at the dosing on record, read with the drug's coverage review under the member's Utilization Management Program:

1. when a dose-change override for the drug was granted on or after the date of the lost supply, the days of the lost supply left on the effective date of the drug's quantity-limit approval in force are re-counted at that approval's quantity per 30 days (multiplied by the lost supply's quantity per 30 days and divided by the approved one, rounded down to whole days) and the days from that effective date to today are taken off;
2. when instead a quantity-limit exception case for the drug opened after the date of the lost supply is still awaiting decision, the days of the lost supply left on the date that case was opened are re-counted at the quantity per 30 days the case requests (multiplied by the lost supply's quantity per 30 days and divided by the requested one, rounded down to whole days) and the days from that date to today are taken off;
3. otherwise the lost days are the days not yet run out today at the lost supply's own dosing.

**Terms.** The dose-change override looked at is the most recent one granted on the benefit for the drug. The quantity-limit approval is the drug's most recent one on the Utilization Management Program records. The case is the most recently opened quantity-limit exception case for the drug, awaiting decision while neither approved, denied nor withdrawn. The lost supply's quantity per 30 days is its quantity multiplied by 30 and divided by its days supply. The days of the lost supply left on a date are the days from that date to the day its days supply runs out, counted from the day its days start, never below zero.

## Worked example (hypothetical): a dose-change override on record

Lost supply: retail fill of 30 tablets for 30 days, date of service day 0, so 30 per 30 days. Quantity-limit approval effective day 10 at 60 per 30 days. Dose-change override granted day 12. Today is day 15.

| Step | Figure |
|---|---|
| Days left on day 10 | 30 less 10: 20 |
| Re-counted at 60 per 30 days | 20 multiplied by 30, divided by 60: 10 |
| Days from day 10 to today | 5 |
| Lost days | 10 less 5: 5 |

At the lost supply's own dosing the same fill would have 15 days not yet run out today.

## Worked example (hypothetical): a pending case

Same fill; no dose-change override on or after day 0; a quantity-limit exception case opened day 6 requesting 45 per 30 days is awaiting decision; today is day 15. Days left on day 6: 24. Re-counted: 24 multiplied by 30, divided by 45, is 16, rounded down to 16. Less the 9 days from day 6 to today: 7 lost days.
